title: Swapface Review and Alternatives (2026): 6 Tools With Better Video and No Watermarks
summary: Understand Swapface's local desktop workflow and compare six current alternatives for browser, API, mobile, multi-face and local face swapping.
body_markdown:
## Quick answer


**Swapface is a desktop face-swapping application for live streams, video calls, saved video and images.**


Choose it when local desktop processing and real-time camera output matter. If you want a browser upload instead, start with Magic Hour or DeepSwap; use FaceFusion for an open local workflow, AKOOL for API or live production, Reface for a consumer mobile route, or Remaker for another browser option.


Swapface at swapface.org and SwapFaces.ai are different products. Verify the domain before installing software, signing in or comparing prices. Product pages were checked September 13, 2026. We did not run a retained visual-quality benchmark, so this guide compares workflow and documented capability rather than declaring a universal output winner.


For a current market-level shortlist, compare[eight AI face-swap tools by workflow](https://magichour.ai/blog/ai-face-swap-tools) .


Magic Hour publishes this guide and includes its own product in the comparison. Treat the recommendations as editorial guidance from a vendor, and verify the linked first-party product details and your own output requirements before choosing a tool.


## Swapface at a glance


-


**Use it for:** local desktop image, video and live-stream face replacement.


-


**Main tradeoff:** installation and hardware matter more than in a hosted browser workflow.


-


**Before installing:** confirm the operating system, GPU requirements, download source, license and current pricing on swapface.org.


-


**Do not confuse it with:** SwapFaces.ai, a separate hosted product with its own account and terms.


Swapface interface captured for the earlier review. Use the current official download page for requirements and pricing; interface details can change.

### Try a browser face swap first


Use a short, well-lit clip and a clear replacement portrait. Review identity, edges, turns and temporary obstructions before committing a longer video.


[Try Face Swap](https://magichour.ai/products/face-swap)


## 1. Magic Hour: browser photo, video and GIF workflows


[Magic Hour Face Swap](https://magichour.ai/products/face-swap) runs in a browser and accepts your own media. Current guest routes provide five photo swaps per day and a shared allowance of three video or GIF generations per day without signup. Photo downloads are watermark-free; free video and GIF outputs include a watermark.


Choose the route by source: photo, video, GIF or multiple people. Magic Hour also provides a developer API. Signed-in editors and APIs use separate credit and plan rules, so do not infer production pricing from the guest allowance.


Magic Hour browser workflow captured for the earlier review. Current limits above come from the product and help documentation, not the screenshot.


## 2. DeepSwap: hosted photo, video and GIF uploads


[DeepSwap](https://www.deepswap.ai/) is a hosted browser option for images, videos and GIFs. It is useful when you want to upload a saved file without managing local models or a desktop camera pipeline.


Its current pricing page uses credits and plan-specific benefits. Check the supported length, file size, number of faces, credit estimate and refund terms before uploading a long video.


DeepSwap interface captured for the earlier review. Treat it as workflow context, not proof of current pricing or output quality.


## 3. FaceFusion: local control and open source


[FaceFusion](https://facefusion.io/) is an open-source local face-manipulation project for images and video. The official site links the source repository and sells optional Windows and macOS installers. Choose it when local processing and configuration matter more than a hosted one-click flow.


You are responsible for installation, hardware, model files and model-specific licenses. Keep the exact release and settings with each result so the workflow can be reproduced.


## 4. AKOOL: API, batch and live production


[AKOOL Face Swap](https://www.akool.com/apps/faceswap) documents image, video, batch, multi-face and live workflows. Its API documentation separates unified image/video endpoints from specialized routes. Choose it when an engineering or production team needs programmatic or live-camera control.


Verify the specific endpoint, credit quote, maximum input and result-retention period before production. Product-page quality claims are vendor claims unless you test them on your own footage.


## 5. Reface: consumer mobile and web workflows


[Reface](https://reface.ai/) is a consumer face-swap brand with mobile and web experiences. Choose it when templates, casual mobile use or Reface's Unboring web tools match the job.


Confirm that the current route accepts the source and target media you want. Template animation, selfie restyling and swapping a face through an uploaded video are different workflows.


## 6. Remaker: another browser route


[Remaker's photo face swap](https://remaker.ai/face-swap-free/) and its separate video tool provide a browser alternative. It remains relevant because some users want a direct hosted upload without local setup.


Remaker separates photo and video routes and uses different credit units. Read the displayed allowance and estimate on the exact page rather than carrying a photo limit into a video comparison.


## Choose by workflow, not a demo clip


-


**Live camera or streaming:** start with Swapface or AKOOL's documented live workflow and confirm latency on your hardware and network.


-


**One browser upload:** compare Magic Hour, DeepSwap and Remaker on the same short clip.


-


**Local and configurable:** use FaceFusion and record the release, processor, model and settings.


-


**Consumer mobile templates:** inspect Reface's current app and verify that your own target media is supported.


-


**API or batch production:** compare Magic Hour and AKOOL on endpoint behavior, asynchronous jobs, retention, rate limits and accepted-output cost.


## A fair face-swap test


Use a five-to-ten-second clip you have permission to edit. Include a front-facing moment, a head turn, speech, a temporary obstruction and changing light. Use the same replacement portrait. Record attempts, processing cost and human review time, then inspect identity, skin tone, edges, teeth, glasses, hairline and frame-to-frame stability at normal playback speed.


Do not upload a private person's face without permission. Label synthetic or materially altered media when the platform, audience or applicable policy requires it, and never use a face swap to impersonate someone or fabricate an endorsement.

## Swapface system requirements and local processing


Swapface’s current official page offers downloads for Windows and Apple-silicon Macs. Its published Windows baseline is Windows 10 64-bit 22H2 or later, 16 GB RAM, 10 GB of free SSD storage and an NVIDIA RTX 2060 or RTX 3060-class GPU with at least 6 GB of VRAM. The recommended configuration is higher. Check the live requirements before installing because hardware support can change.


The company says processing runs on the user’s device. That can reduce upload exposure and support real-time camera output, but local processing also moves responsibility to your computer. Confirm installer provenance, operating-system permissions, camera routing, model downloads, storage use and the privacy policy before using confidential media.


## How to test Swapface for live video


Test the complete path you will actually use: camera, Swapface, virtual camera if required, streaming or meeting software, encoder and network. Measure end-to-end delay while speaking and turning, then watch the recorded output rather than judging only the preview.


Run at the target resolution and frame rate for at least ten minutes. Watch GPU memory, dropped frames, thermal throttling, audio-video sync and recovery after the face leaves the frame. A short demo can hide failures that appear during a real stream.


## Swapface safety and purchase checklist


Download only from the official domain and verify that the product is Swapface at swapface.org, not the separate SwapFaces.ai web service. Review the current price, license, refund terms, update policy and support route before paying.


Use media you own or have permission to edit. Obtain consent from every identifiable person, avoid deceptive impersonation and disclose synthetic media when viewers could reasonably mistake it for a real event or endorsement.
